harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 successfully. inventory-api is a hardened, enabled systemd service on TCP/8080. batchworker has an immutable 128 MiB per-process virtual-memory limit. Both controls survived the mandatory node restart.
actions_performed: Created dedicated inventory-api and batchworker accounts.
Installed a Python 3 standard-library inventory API without changing packages, OS, or kernel.
Enabled inventory-api.service with systemd hardening and automatic failure recovery.
Allowed only TCP/8080 through runtime and persistent firewalld configuration.
Configured batchworker soft and hard RLIMIT_AS values to 131072 KiB.
Verified a 192 MiB batch allocation fails while the API remains healthy.
Removed temporary test artifacts and restored SELinux labels.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api managed service on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: The validated systemd unit is enabled and active under its dedicated account. Direct requests through NODE_IP return healthy inventory data, and the listener is bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: batchworker limited to 128 MB virtual memory per process without interrupting API
evidence.summary: batchworker receives soft and hard RLIMIT_AS values of 134217728 bytes. A 192 MiB allocation fails with MemoryError, the account cannot raise its hard limit, and the API remains healthy during and after the failure and following restart.

RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remain installed. SELinux remains Enforcing, SSH and firewalld remain active, sshd validates, protected configuration hashes match their baselines, and no temporary test residue remains.

Pre-restart boot identity and healthy state were captured; systemd acknowledged the delayed safe reboot; boot identity changed from d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6 to e35ba686-07a2-4737-b0ac-3decbaf33bba; afterward the system was running with the API, listener, inventory data, memory limit, firewall, SSH, and SELinux recovered and zero failed units.
